title: Geometry-Adaptive Explainer for Faithful Dictionary-Based Interpretability under Distribution Shift
claim: Distribution shift rotates the active subspace away from the trained dictionary, and a training-free realign-and-refit step closes the gap.
layout: 3 panels plus legend, left-to-right, zoom-in inset with dotted callout lines
description: A top banner shows an English sentence on the left, 'The capital of France is Paris.', a blue-to-orange arrow labeled 'Distribution shift', and a French version on the right. Below it, the left panel has a red alert icon and the title 'OOD Shift opens a Faithfulness Gap'. It shows 3D axes with a tilted blue plane (Π_dec / Π_ID) above a flat orange plane (Π_OOD). A red curved arrow joins the planes, and a siren icon sits beside the gap formula Δ(Π_dec)=‖Π_OOD−Π_dec‖_F. The right panel has a green check and the title 'GAE: Realign while preserving feature activations'. Step 1 'Align' shows the blue plane swinging onto a green plane that sits over the orange one. Step 2 'Refit' zooms into a dotted-outline inset where feature vectors rotate toward the OOD directions, with weights 0.35 and 0.8. At the far right is a small grid of token features (city, value, capital, Paris) tied to the French sentence. A legend strip along the bottom explains the four subspace colors.
caption: Faithfulness gap and GAE. Left: distribution shift (illustrated as a language change) rotates the OOD-active subspace ΠOOD away from the ID-trained explainer subspace Πdec ≈ΠID, opening a faithfulness gap ∆(Πdec). Right: GAE uses two steps. Step 1 rotates Πdec onto the estimated OOD-active subspace via orthogonal Procrustes. Step 2 refits feature directions under an alignment penalty to match OOD activations while preserving the original sparse feature activations.
abstract: Mechanistic interpretability aims to explain a model's behavior by identifying causally responsible internal structures. Dictionary-based explainers such as sparse autoencoders and transcoders are a primary tool, but their faithfulness under out-of-distribution (OOD) shift has received little systematic attention. We show that distribution shift rotates the subspace that the model actively uses, misaligning the explainer's dictionary trained on in-distribution (ID) activations. We formalize this misalignment as the faithfulness gap, a geometric distance between the ID dictionary and the OOD-active subspace, and show that it bounds excess OOD projection loss. To reduce this gap, we propose the Geometry-Adaptive Explainer (GAE), which realigns the dictionary with the OOD-active subspace while preserving the original sparse feature activations. This requires only unlabeled OOD activations and no gradient updates. For the adapted dictionary, we also bound the excess projection loss caused by any remaining faithfulness gap. Empirically, GAE even matches or surpasses all training-based baselines in causal faithfulness across multiple models and OOD settings.
